events.title: COBOL specifications submitted
events.summary: The CODASYL short-range committee submitted the first COBOL language specifications for business data processing.
events.about: COBOL was for business records on mainframes — readable English-like syntax for payroll, banking, insurance, and government systems. Example jobs: processing millions of transactions, printing statements, and batch reporting. A large share of global financial back-office code still runs on COBOL.

narrative.whyChosen: COBOL standardized how industries described business logic in portable, readable programs.
narrative.whyImportant: DoD pressure made COBOL available across vendors, proving cross-machine business languages could work.
narrative.problemSolved: Every manufacturer had incompatible data-processing languages; COBOL aimed for one common business language.

sources.title: CODASYL — COBOL Report (April 1960, specs dated Dec 1959)
